title: Grain Marketing Contracts: Delayed Price Terms by Marketing Programme
content:
Bushels standing unpriced on Grain Marketing Contracts are carried on terms set by the programme the contract is written on. Four terms are catalogued: the free days a parcel carries before the service charge runs, the monthly rate, the floor under the charge on any one parcel, and the longest a parcel may stand unpriced.

| Programme | Free days before the charge runs | Monthly rate (USD per bushel per thirty-day month) | Floor on any one parcel (USD) | Longest a parcel may stand unpriced (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Spot Cash Delivery Ticket | 0 | 0.000 | 0.00 | 0 |
| Forward Cash Sale Contract | 0 | 0.000 | 0.00 | 0 |
| Basis Fixed Contract | 15 | 0.040 | 20.00 | 240 |
| Hedge-to-Arrive Contract | 10 | 0.045 | 25.00 | 210 |
| Delayed Price Agreement | 30 | 0.050 | 15.00 | 300 |
| Minimum Price Contract | 10 | 0.045 | 25.00 | 180 |
| Managed Accumulator Program | 10 | 0.040 | 25.00 | 180 |

The Spot Cash Delivery Ticket and the Forward Cash Sale Contract admit no parcel into the unpriced position, and every delayed price term on those two programmes is accordingly nil.

## Read as the member's terms

The free days are the calendar days a parcel carries free of the service charge. The monthly rate is the charge per bushel for each thirty-day month of carry. The floor is the least the cooperative will take on any one parcel. The longest period is the outside limit within which bushels standing unpriced are to be priced.

The most generous free period in the catalogue is the 30 days carried by the Delayed Price Agreement, which also carries the longest unpriced period at 300 calendar days and the highest monthly rate at 0.050 per bushel. The Basis Fixed Contract carries 15 free days, a rate of 0.040, a floor of 20.00 and an outside limit of 240 calendar days.
